item.title: Barry Manilow Postpones May Las Vegas Shows Amid Cancer Recovery
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our show, I'm your host. Today, we're bringing you an update on music legend Barry Manilow. The 82-year-old singer has been on the path to recovery after undergoing lung cancer surgery, and he's just shared some news with his fans.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: In an Instagram post, Manilow revealed that he's making great progress, but unfortunately, he won't be able to perform his May residency dates in Las Vegas. However, he's optimistic about returning to the Westgate stage in July.
[Short pause]
Host: Manilow did confirm that he'll be ready to perform his June arena shows in the UK, and his Las Vegas residency is scheduled to run through December. This is the latest update in a series of postponements since he announced his Stage 1 lung cancer diagnosis in December 2025.
[Soft music continues]
Host: Despite the setbacks, Manilow remains determined to get back on stage. With a career spanning over five decades, he's had an incredible run, selling over 85 million albums worldwide and scoring 13 No. 1 singles on the Adult Contemporary chart.
[Short pause]
Host: And in some exciting news, his new single "Once Before I Go" recently became a top 10 hit, making him the only artist to have a hit in six consecutive decades. His new album "What a Time" is due out on June 5th.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. We wish Barry Manilow a continued recovery and look forward to his return to the stage. Thanks for tuning in.
